bounded_pi_report_statement: In Shreve, Ohio, the matched 2024 municipality-cycle candidate draws both rates from the same municipal wage ordinance: $22.00 per hour for part-time police officers and $16.00 per hour for a part-time utility clerk. On the current normalized hourly basis, the safety-side rate is $6.00 per hour higher, or 37.5% above the clerk rate. This is bounded local documentary evidence and requires substantive validation of occupational and work-schedule comparability before analytic use; it is not a final wage-gap estimate, nationally representative result, prevalence claim, or causal finding.
caveat_text: Same-document hourly rates are validated, but duties, experience, hours, and other job requirements are not matched; use only as a bounded local documentary comparison.
caveats: ["The comparison is between a group-wide part-time police rate and the rate for one part-time utility-clerk position.", "The ordinance does not establish equivalence in duties, experience, schedule, or hiring requirements across the two occupations.", "The utility-clerk line caps work at 28 hours; the police line does not state an hours cap on the same page.", "The comparison is a bounded local documentary rate difference, not a final wage-gap estimate or a nationally representative result."]
effective_period_evidence: Village of Shreve Ordinance No. 10-2024, passed October 21, 2024, replaces prior pay schedules and restates the 2024 wage schedule; both rates appear in Exhibit A, Section 1.
forbidden_claim_warning: Do not write 'the wage gap is 37.5%' or infer a general safety premium, national prevalence, policy effect, or causal relationship.
